readings: Using the town or city of the customer who placed the order behind each invoice line item: first, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values; then average those per town. Which towns have an average cost ratio above the average across all towns? Show the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how far its ratio is above the cross-town average, without rounding.
queries:
WITH item_town AS (
    SELECT
        ili.order_item_id,
        c.town_city AS town,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(1.0 * ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS average_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town,
        AVG(average_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(average_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM item_town
    GROUP BY town
)
SELECT
    town,
    average_price,
    average_ratio,
    average_ratio - (SELECT AVG(average_ratio) FROM town_averages) AS ratio_above_average
FROM town_averages
WHERE average_ratio > (SELECT AVG(average_ratio) FROM town_averages)
